item.title: Midterms Pit Republican Cash Machine Against Democratic Fury
item.description: Money may talk, but the discontents of voters ring loud
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Fed Raises Rates as Warsh Bucks Trump to Contain Inflation: Fed Special
item.description: Bloomberg's Tom Keene, Jonathan Ferro and Lisa Abramowicz discuss remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh after the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since 2023. The FOMC voted unanimously to raise rates by 25 basis points and the dot plot showed many Fed officials signaling support for further hikes. The move to hike rates goes in the face of prolonged pressure from President Trump to lower rates. Warsh said 'I’ve got nothing for you on on a discussion with the president' when asked by reporters. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dutta Expects Fed to Hike Rates More Than Once From Here
item.description: Neil Dutta of Renaissance Macro Economic Research expects the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates more than once from here. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New US Space Weapon Adds to Arsenal to Counter Russia, China
item.description: The revelation by the Air Force this week that the US now has a weapon in space stoked speculation — but few answers — about the weapon’s capability.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Trump’s AI Defense Defies Voter Unease Ahead of Midterms
item.description: Bloomberg's Michael Shepard joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Senior Trump administration officials met Tuesday with Anthropic’s top Washington executive to discuss AI's safety risks. Anthropic’s IPO preparations came as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Elon Musk on Saturday all voiced the need to slow the pace of AI development due to escalating risks from the technology. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Chairman Warsh Calls Rate Hike a 'Sober' Decision
item.description: "The decision we made today was a sober decision, serious decision, responsible decision, one that we have been preparing for and thinking about in my hundred and ten or twenty days here," Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said after the FOMC raised interest rates by a quarter percentage point. He speaks in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Top Trump Aide Wiles Says She’s Cancer Free After Treatment
item.description: President Donald Trump’s chief of staff, Susie Wiles, announced she is “cancer free” after undergoing treatment for breast cancer this year.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Fed Removed Dose of Accommodation With Hike, Chairman Warsh Says
item.description: “We removed a dose of accommodation,” Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says after policymakers raised interest rates by a quarter percentage point. He speaks in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: House Holds Leon Black in Contempt in Epstein Subpoena Clash
item.description: The US House voted to hold billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress for failure to comply with two subpoenas issued in a committee’s investigation into sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Warsh Faces Markets and Trump
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz preview the Federal Reserve's rate decision. On today's show, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Unleash Prosperity Co-Founder Stephen Moore. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Sector Not Giving Up on Congress: Blockchain Association
item.description: Senators from both parties blocked a landmark digital asset market structure bill in a procedural vote, sending crypto stocks tumbling. The bill would have handed the CFTC the primary authority to regulate the digital assets industry, but failed to advance with a vote of 49-50. Blockchain Association CEO Summer Mersinger says she is still optimistic that crypto will eventually get the regulatory framework it needs. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canadians Supportive of Closer Europe Ties Amid US Tension
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s effort to formalize a deeper relationship with Europe is broadly supported by Canadians, who have grown increasingly disillusioned with the US as their government faces hostility from President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Nojoud Al Mallees and Laura Osman

item.title: Why the World Is Watching the Yen
item.description: The Japanese yen is trading at levels not seen since the 1980s. It’s good news for tourists but a headache for the economy. Now, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting involved. Here’s why. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Alberta Study Finds Canada Split Would Damage Province’s Economy
item.description: Separating from Canada would cause significant economic damage to Alberta from which it would take years to recover, according to a study commissioned by the province’s government.
item.dc:creator: Iain Boekhoff

item.title: Scottish Parliament Vows to Set Tighter Rules on Data Centers
item.description: Scotland’s parliament agreed to tighten the rules on building new data centers, in a sign of growing opposition to the UK’s artificial intelligence ambitions.
item.dc:creator: Marion Dakers

item.title: Sweden’s Center-Left Projected to Win Election by One Seat
item.description: Sweden’s center-left opposition bloc is projected to win Sunday’s tight general election by one seat after days of limbo, effectively closing off — for now — the prospect of the far-right entering government.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Duxbury

item.title: US-Canada Rupture Is a Lesson in Poor Leadership Says Mukunda
item.description: Trade talks between the US and Canada broke down at the last minute late last month, resulting in tariffs and an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America. The breakdown was due to nobody on the American side being able to say who had the authority to make a deal stick, as officials pursued incompatible policies. Gautam Mukunda Bloomberg Opinion Columnist and Yale School of Management Lecturer joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Blockade Costs Are Draining America’s Global Military Power
item.description: As US President Donald Trump tries to force Iran into submission, a naval blockade is proving to be his tool of choice. But the operation is stretching the American military to its limit, exhausting troops and weakening Washington’s position elsewhere in the world, including Asia. Bloomberg's Becca Wasser joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meloni to Abolish Italy Vehicle Ownership Tax to Woo Voters
item.description: Giorgia Meloni’s government introduced a sweeping vehicle ownership tax cut, as the Italian premier seeks to stem the impact of the energy crisis on consumers ahead of a general election next year.
item.dc:creator: Donato Paolo Mancini and Alberto Brambilla

item.title: What Would Canada Having EU ‘Associate Member’ Status Mean for US Relations?
item.description: To soften the blow from its trade standoff with the US, Canada needs to boost economic ties with other parts of the world. Prime Minister Mark Carney has made it clear he wants a closer relationship with the European Union. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s offer to make Canada an “associate member” of the world’s most powerful trading bloc during her annual speech to the European Parliament on Sept. 16 went further than many had expected.
